plain_description: Turn any AI image model into an animation generator with zero extra training. AnimateDiff plugs into your existing Stable Diffusion workflow to add motion, creating smooth videos from still images. The bottom line: bring your AI-generated visuals to life in minutes.
technical_description: AnimateDiff is a PyTorch-based motion module for Stable Diffusion that enables text-to-video generation by inserting learnable temporal layers into frozen text-to-image models. The architecture supports multiple model versions (v1–v3, SDXL-beta) with extended control via MotionLoRA for camera movements and SparseCtrl encoders for RGB/sketch conditioning. Inference runs locally through Python scripts or a Gradio interface, with checkpoint caching for offline operation. Training pipelines are included for custom motion module and MotionLoRA development. The codebase integrates with the HuggingFace Diffusers library.
title: AnimateDiff

body: text and image to video generation: CogVideoX (2024) and CogVideo (ICLR 2023)
plain_description: Create professional videos from text or images with CogVideoX — an open-source AI model that runs on a single consumer GPU. Fine-tune it for your brand's unique style without expensive cloud services. The bottom line: high-quality, customized video content at a fraction of the cost.
technical_description: CogVideoX is a text-to-video and image-to-video generation model built on a diffusion transformer (DiT) architecture. The project provides inference and fine-tuning code via the Hugging Face Diffusers library and the SwissArmyTransformer (SAT) framework. Models are available at 2B and 5B parameter scales and support BF16, FP16, INT8, and FP8 precision modes. Integration is supported through Python API, CLI, Gradio web UI, and third-party frameworks including ComfyUI and xDiT.
title: CogVideoX

body: HunyuanVideo: A Systematic Framework For Large Video Generation Model
plain_description: Generate high-quality videos from text descriptions with HunyuanVideo, Tencent's open-source foundation model that outperforms leading commercial alternatives like Runway Gen-3 and Luma 1.6. It handles everything from simple prompts to complex scenes with superior motion quality and visual fidelity. The bottom line: create production-ready video content without the cost of closed-source solutions.
technical_description: HunyuanVideo is an open-source video generation framework implementing a diffusion transformer architecture with over 13 billion parameters. It operates on a spatial-temporally compressed latent space via a Causal 3D VAE and uses a Dual-stream to Single-stream hybrid transformer design with Full Attention. Text conditioning employs a finetuned Multimodal Large Language Model with bidirectional token refinement. The runtime requires an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA, minimum 45 GB GPU memory (60 GB for 720p), and supports Docker deployment, Gradio web interface, FP8 quantization, and parallel multi-GPU inference via xDiT with Unified Sequence Parallelism.
title: HunyuanVideo

plain_description: Generate high-quality, realistic videos with synchronized audio from text or images. LTX-Video is a powerful video generation model that creates up to 4K resolution footage at 50 FPS, with built-in audio synchronization and multiple creative controls.
technical_description: LTX-Video is a DiT-based video generation foundation model supporting text-to-video, image-to-video, multi-keyframe conditioning, video extension, and video-to-video transformations. It uses a latent diffusion architecture with spatiotemporal guidance and supports multiple model variants (2B and 13B parameters) with distilled and FP8 quantized versions for reduced VRAM usage and faster inference. The model is implemented in Python with PyTorch, integrates with ComfyUI and HuggingFace Diffusers, and provides a Python library API via `ltx_video.inference`. Inference requires NVIDIA GPUs with CUDA 12.2+ or Apple Silicon via MPS, with optional FP8 kernel support for Ada-generation GPUs.
title: LTX-Video

body: The best OSS video generation models, created by Genmo
plain_description: The big picture: Genmo's Mochi 1 brings high-quality video generation to open source, letting you create custom videos on your own hardware with no per-generation fees. Fine-tune it on your own footage using LoRA adapters, and run it through a simple web interface or programmatic API. The bottom line: professional video generation without vendor lock-in or recurring API costs.
technical_description: Mochi 1 is a 10-billion-parameter open-source diffusion model for text-to-video generation, built on the Asymmetric Diffusion Transformer (AsymmDiT) architecture with 48 layers, 24 attention heads, and separate MLP streams for visual (3072-dim) and text (1536-dim) tokens. The accompanying AsymmVAE provides causal 128x spatiotemporal compression via an asymmetric encoder-decoder design. Inference runs through PyTorch with optional flash attention, requiring approximately 60 GB VRAM for single-GPU operation with support for multi-GPU model parallelism. The repository exposes a composable Python pipeline API, a CLI for batch generation, and a Gradio web interface. LoRA fine-tuning is supported on H100 or A100 80 GB GPUs via a dedicated trainer, with safetensors checkpoint format.
title: Mochi 1

body: Open-Sora: Democratizing Efficient Video Production for All
plain_description: The big picture: Open-Sora gives you professional-quality AI video generation from text prompts — without the six-figure licensing fees of proprietary tools. Here's why it matters: it handles text-to-video, image-to-video, and video editing in one open-source platform that rivals commercial solutions. The bottom line: production-grade video generation at a fraction of the enterprise cost.
technical_description: Open-Sora is an open-source video generation framework built on diffusion transformer (DiT) architecture. The 11B-parameter v2.0 model supports text-to-video and image-to-video generation at up to 768px resolution using 3D-VAE encoding, rectified flow, and score conditioning. Inference runs via torchrun on single or multi-GPU NVIDIA H100/H800 clusters, accelerated by ColossalAI tensor and sequence parallelism. Training and fine-tuning scripts are provided for custom model development. Additional capabilities include motion score control, prompt refinement through OpenAI API integration, and variable aspect ratio generation. The project is distributed as a Python package via pip with CUDA-dependent runtime requirements.
title: Open-Sora

body: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
plain_description: Generate studio-quality videos from text descriptions or images using AI — without needing a Hollywood budget. Wan2.1 runs on standard consumer graphics cards (as low as 8GB VRAM), making professional video generation accessible to small teams and individual creators. It handles text-to-video, image-to-video, video editing, and text-to-image in a single unified model.
technical_description: Wan2.1 is an open-source suite of video foundation models built on a diffusion transformer (DiT) architecture with flow matching. The model uses a 3D causal VAE (Wan-VAE) for spatio-temporal compression and a T5 encoder for multilingual text conditioning. It supports multiple generative tasks including text-to-video, image-to-video, video editing, text-to-image, and video-to-audio across 1.3B and 14B parameter variants. Inference runs on NVIDIA GPUs via PyTorch, with integrations available for Diffusers, ComfyUI, and Gradio, and supports multi-GPU distributed inference through FSDP and xDiT USP.
title: Wan2.1
